0: Those whose intellect has transcended existence and non-existence, being without support —
1: by them the profound, groundless meaning of dependent origination (<s>pratyayārtha</s>) is realized.
3: Those who do not see reality (<s>atattvadarśins</s>) conceive of both <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>;
4: those who see reality (<s>tattvadarśins</s>) conceive of neither <s>saṃsāra</s> nor <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
5: <s>Nirvāṇa</s> and becoming (<s>bhava</s>) — this duality does not exist;
6: the thorough knowledge of becoming itself is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>.
8: Whatever arises having obtained such-and-such [conditions], that has not arisen by its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>);
9: that which has not arisen by its own nature — how can it be called 'arisen'?
11: At first, one who investigates reality should say 'everything exists';
12: afterward, for one who has understood the meaning, who is free from attachment — [there is] detachment.
14: Just as 'mine' and 'I' were spoken by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) according to practical necessity,
15: so too the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements) were spoken according to practical necessity.
16: The great elements and so forth are said to be subsumed in consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>);
17: when that knowledge ceases, are they not falsely constructed?
19: That whose arising depends on causes, whose persistence is not without conditions,
20: whose cessation is from the absence of conditions — how is that understood as 'existing'?
22: Born from attachment and aversion, the embrace of intensely corrupt views,
23: and the disputes that arise from them — [all occur] when there is acceptance of [inherent] existence.
24: That [acceptance of existence] is the cause of all [wrong] views; without it, <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) do not arise;
25: therefore, when it is thoroughly known, views and afflictions are completely exhausted.
26: How is that thoroughly known? — Through seeing dependent origination (<s>pratītyotpāda</s>);
27: the best among those who know reality declared that what is dependently arisen is unborn.
29: Fools are attached to forms; the mediocre develop dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>);
30: those of supreme wisdom, who know the essential nature [of forms], are liberated.
